message.content:
Single-annotator gold-set construction for domain-specific NLP tasks like philosophical text and ontology resolution lacks comprehensive 2024-2026 published protocols explicitly targeting solo-rater bias mitigation; available methodologies emphasize LLM-assisted validation and decomposition to approximate multi-annotator reliability when only one human is feasible.[1][4]

### Protocols for Single-Annotator Scenarios
- **LLM-as-Judge for Bias Mitigation**: In domain-specific knowledge extraction (e.g., ontology-aligned triples from reports), combine human-annotated triples with an **LLM-as-Judge protocol** to counter position bias in reference-free scoring; this hybrid approach ensures real-world relevance without additional humans.[1]
- **Atomic Decomposition and LLM Parsing**: Decompose text into atomic units (e.g., claims or triples) using a single powerful LLM like Qwen3-235B for extraction, classification (e.g., novelty, soundness), and semantic parsing; apply linguistic principles like causal decomposition and coreference resolution to create structured gold sets, decoupling fields like strengths/weaknesses for consistency.[4]
- **Partial Annotation Strategies**: Use word-based partial annotation to efficiently build corpora with one annotator, focusing effort on high-value tokens rather than full sentences; this reduces bias by prioritizing uncertain or domain-critical elements (e.g., philosophical entities or ontology links).[3]
No protocols were found specifically for philosophical text or ontology resolution; inference from ontology triple extraction suggests adaptation via domain prompts, which improved accuracy by 44.2% and reduced hallucinations by 22.5%.[1]

### LLM-as-Second-Annotator Approaches (Claude/GPT/Gemini)
- **Effectiveness and Disagreement Adjudication**: LLM-as-Judge (e.g., Qwen3-235B) effectively decomposes and classifies atomic claims in reviews, enabling single-annotator gold sets; no direct comparisons for Claude/GPT/Gemini or explicit disagreement adjudication protocols (e.g., majority vote or calibration) in 2024-2026 results.[4] In knowledge graph tasks, ontology-aligned prompts with LLM judging mitigate bias without naming specific models.[1]
- **Unknowns**: Minimum agreement thresholds (e.g., LLM-human Kappa >0.6) and adjudication specifics (e.g., retry on disagreement) are not detailed; no evidence of Claude/GPT/Gemini benchmarks here.

### Statistical Floors and F1 Measurements
No 2024-2026 sources specify **minimum F1 floors** for models evaluated against single-annotator gold sets; reliability is inferred via LLM-human hybrid metrics like position bias reduction, but quantitative floors (e.g., F1>0.7 as statistical baseline) remain unknown.[1][4]

### Recent Papers on LLM-Judge Calibration
- **TextMineX (NEC Labs, ~2025)**: Bias-aware framework with human-LLM triples for ontology extraction; calibrates via position bias mitigation.[1]
- **AI Reviews Benchmark (arXiv 2604.19502v2, 2026)**: Qwen3-235B for atomic decomposition/classification in argumentative text; implies calibration through linguistic principles, but no explicit human-gold metrics.[4]
- Related: SYNQA (NEC, ~2025) uses LLMs for QA synthesis with attribution, validated via user studies on fine-tuned LMs.[1]
No 2024-2026 papers directly on LLM-judge calibration against single-annotator philosophical/ontology gold; prefer these for production hardening due to recency and domain alignment. Flag: Search misses ICLR 2024 specifics[5]; deeper arXiv mining needed for F1 thresholds.
